newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says EMU would be advantage for firms.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says EMU would be advantage for firms.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp president Hiroshi Okuda said on Thursday that a single currency would be a significant advantage for firms operating in Europe and that this was one factor to consider in making investment decisions.

Okuda's comments, in a statement released by Toyota, came a day after he sparked a political furore in Britain by saying that the firm may shift its investment focus away from Britain if the country stays outside a single European currency.

In his statement, Okuda did not refer to the comments he made to reporters at a reception on Wednesday, but stressed that Toyota's policy of considering future British investment as one of its options in Europe has "not changed at all".
"(The) Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC) position regarding necessary future investment in Europe is now under study and nothing has been decided," Okuda's statement said.
But he said European economic and monetary union (EMU) was one of the "basic business factors" which Toyota takes into account in making investment decisions.

"Generally speaking, regarding companies which operate in Europe, a unifed currency would reduce currency exchange-rate fluctuations and risk and would be a significant advantage," the statement said.
